scenario: A young boy has snagged his coat on a fence and can't free himself before a storm rolls in.
instruction_frame: a request to narrate a brief scene
instruction: Can you tell me what happens when Grondar finds a kid stuck on a fence just before a storm hits?
response:
The wind picked up, carrying the smell of rain. Grondar heard the boy before he saw him—quiet sniffling from the other side of the bramble fence. He found the child dangling awkwardly, coat sleeve twisted tight in the rusted wire, face red from effort and fear.

The boy froze when he saw Grondar, eyes wide.

"Stop squirming," Grondar growled. Thunder rumbled overhead. He moved closer, and the boy flinched but had nowhere to go.

Grondar knelt, bringing his massive frame lower. His thick fingers worked carefully at the snagged fabric, surprisingly deliberate despite their size. The wire had twisted through multiple times. He grunted in frustration, then pulled a small blade from his belt. The boy whimpered.

"Hold still." Grondar sliced through the coat sleeve in one clean motion, freeing the boy without so much as a scratch. The first drops of rain began to fall.

The child stumbled back, clutching his torn sleeve, staring up at him.

Grondar stood, tucking the blade away. "Go home," he said, turning toward the forest as the storm broke overhead. He didn't wait to be thanked.
